name: hard-flick-settle-timing
description: extends the frame-capture settle-timing diagnostic (build/scenarios/scrub-settle-timing.json) with a genuinely hard flick, because that fixture's own fast-flick (dx=-45, phase_ms=120) never crossed commitSettleDampingAnchorVelocity (6 progress/s) - measured commitScrub initialVelocity was only 0.85-1.38 progress/s, so the velocity-hardened settle-damping branch was never exercised by any gesture the harness could synthesize. This is a scenario-JSON-only change: cgevent's scroll primitive already accepts arbitrary dx/phase_ms (build/vm-tools/cgevent.swift splits totalDeltaX evenly across phase_ms/step_ms with no upper bound), so no tool code change was needed. Same fixture, startup space, and 3-gesture dance as scrub-settle-timing.json - identical gentle drag (dx=90 phase_ms=900 momentum_ms=0, low velocity by design, the baseline) - but the fast-flick's dx is raised from -45 to -450 at the same phase_ms=120/momentum_ms=300 shape, targeting a nominal dx*1000/phase_ms of 3750pt/s: On the -45/120 fixture the actual/nominal ratio measured 0.455-0.735 across two runs (170.78 and 275.75pt/s against a 375pt/s nominal), so this dx gives an expected actual range of ~1700-2760pt/s (8.5-13.8 progress/s at width 200) - comfortably above the 1200pt/s (6 progress/s) anchor even at the worst observed ratio. wip: true (diagnostic/measurement helper, not a regression gate, same as its parent scenario); run by explicit name, not swept by `all`. CONFOUND REMOVAL: the first VM run of this fixture found the gentle-drag capture's settle signal masked by a pixel burst arriving 1.1-1.2s late, matching the known cold-VM-runloop-lag window (the gentle drag was structurally the first gesture, ~3.8s after launch). Fixed by inserting an uncaptured warm-up round trip (Elsewhere -> Editing -> Elsewhere, same dx=-90/90 phase_ms=900 momentum_ms=0 shape as the existing bridge hop) ahead of the gentle-drag capture, each leg gated by wait_vlog on its destination's own tab-url line so the runloop is provably caught up before the capture window opens - not a longer fixed settle, which is insufficient on a cold VM (fixed sleeps assume event processing keeps pace with wall clock; it does not, right after a cold restore). Reordering the two captures instead (hard-flick first) was rejected: it would only TRANSFER the cold-launch confound onto the hard-flick capture, whose settle is the one measurement already proven clean by this exact bridge-hop-then-capture pattern. The round trip returns to Elsewhere so the gentle-drag capture below, and everything after it, is byte-for-byte unchanged.

OBJECTIVE PROOF the gentle drag actually committed a workspace change (Third's tab, cold at launch)

OBJECTIVE PROOF the hard flick actually committed a workspace change (Editing's tab, cold at launch)
